record_identity.title: Mathspace breach exposed personal data of more than one million users in Australia and New Zealand

incident_identity.date_basis: Mathspace states that unauthorised access to its self-hosted Metabase reporting system dated back to 10 August 2026, that information was downloaded from its Australian reporting database on 27 August, and that it confirmed the breach on 3 September 2026.

summary: Mathspace disclosed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its self-hosted Metabase reporting system, obtained administrator access without a legitimate login, and downloaded personal information from its Australian reporting database. Mathspace identified 1,079,819 affected people across Australia and New Zealand, including students, parents or guardians, teachers and Mathspace staff. Exposed fields included names, usernames, email addresses and account metadata. Mathspace states that academic records, assessment results, passwords, authentication tokens, SSO credentials and API credentials were not exposed. After reviewing logs, Mathspace confirmed the breach on 3 September and disabled the affected reporting access. It notified schools and regulators on 4 September and began individual notices on 6 September. Its 8 September update clarified that earlier communications had omitted some exposed account details; recovery checks and notifications were still continuing.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Mathspace's own breach notice states that Metabase published a critical security advisory and patched versions on 6 August 2026, but Mathspace's vulnerability-notification process did not identify and escalate the advisory. Unauthorised access was later traced to 10 August, data was downloaded on 27 August, the Metabase instance was updated on 29 August, and Mathspace confirmed the compromise on 3 September after reviewing historical logs. Mathspace also states that, when it updated the instance, it did not complete additional compromise checks recommended for potentially affected systems. ABC News independently reported the breach and affected population. The 8 September update corrects earlier disclosure of exposed fields. It reports no evidence of subsequent publication or misuse, rather than establishing none occurred. Taking Metabase offline and revoking its access are achieved containment steps; notification and recovery checks remained ongoing.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a large-scale confidentiality breach involving an education platform's internal reporting environment and retained personal data. The evidence supports a chain involving delayed response to a critical vulnerability advisory and incomplete assurance after disclosure, but it does not isolate whether patch governance, monitoring, access control or data-retention practice was the decisive technical mechanism. The critical-advisory notification failure and the affirmative historical log/reconstruction successes are retained as distinct stages. Conventional reporting-database logs are not automatically evidence of model-input/output, GAI incident or agent governance controls. The preserved occurrence does not establish an affected AI lifecycle process or autonomous system. The reviewed AI-specific external requirements are therefore not relevant to this reporting-database breach. Mathspace’s historical logs establish unauthorised access and download of personal records from its reporting database. This crosses the records’ confidentiality boundary independently of subsequent misuse. Credentials were expressly excluded from the corrected exposed-field list, so this does not support a secret-custody finding.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The incident is governance-significant because it affected more than one million people, including students, across Australian and New Zealand education contexts. It highlights the consequences of delayed security-advisory escalation, retained reporting access to large personal-data populations, and incomplete compromise checks following a critical vulnerability disclosure.
assessment_boundaries: The identity and motive of the attacker remain unknown in the reviewed public evidence.
Mathspace reports no evidence so far that the exposed information has been published, distributed, sold or otherwise misused.
No academic records, learning activities, assessment results, password hashes, authentication tokens, SSO credentials or API credentials are reported as exposed.
The exposed records did not directly include school-account linkage, although identifiable school email domains may make school association inferable in some cases.
VIGIL records the disclosed vulnerability-management and compromise-detection chronology without inferring negligence, legal liability or regulatory breach findings.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 6 August, Metabase published a critical advisory and patched versions. Mathspace says its existing vulnerability-notification process did not identify or escalate that advisory.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An applicable advisory must activate the defined notification process.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The published critical advisory satisfied the process trigger, but the control did not activate before exploitation and the later update was not followed by all recommended compromise checks.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Mathspace later traced unauthorised administrator access without legitimate login to 10 August AEST.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An access occurrence precedes later discovery.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Information was downloaded from the Australian reporting database on 27 August.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Initial access and the later download are separate material actions.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The attacker downloaded personal information from Mathspace’s reporting database. The affected records were restricted school-user information, not public statistics.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 29 August, Mathspace updated Metabase after a later notice, but omitted recommended compromise checks.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Patching does not establish that an earlier compromise was absent.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Historical log review confirmed the pre-update compromise on 3 September and reconstructed access and download timing.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Capture and reconstruction are distinct supported properties of the same retrospective review.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Historical logs preserved the unauthorised-access and download events sufficiently for the later compromise to be identified.
The retained logs allowed the key access and download chronology to be reconstructed, including the sequence of unauthorised access and later data download.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 3 September, Mathspace took Metabase offline, revoked its API keys, disabled its Australian and US Snowflake access accounts, changed database passwords and preserved investigation copies.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Containment and evidence preservation do not demonstrate completed system recovery.

clauses.source_paraphrase: School contacts and regulators were notified on 4 September. Individual notifications began on 6 September, earlier than the schedule initially given to schools.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: School coordination, regulator reporting and individual notices have different recipients and dates.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The 8 September update reported 1,079,819 affected people and clarified account metadata omitted from earlier communications. Academic records and authentication credentials were excluded. It reported no evidence of later misuse; individual notices and recovery checks remained ongoing.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Corrected disclosure scope and unfinished response work remain material.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy re-adjudication identifies Required Control Non-Activation as the primary structural mechanism. Mathspace's first-party disclosure states that a critical Metabase security advisory and patched versions were published, that Mathspace's vulnerability-notification process did not identify and escalate the advisory, and that the vulnerable instance remained exposed before unauthorised access and data download. The same disclosure separately states that recommended compromise checks were not completed when the instance was later updated. The classification is bounded to the missed applicable vulnerability-management control and does not treat the breach, attacker conduct, affected population or harm severity as taxonomy membership by themselves. Mathspace’s historical logs establish unauthorised access and download of personal records from its reporting database. This crosses the records’ confidentiality boundary independently of subsequent misuse. Credentials were expressly excluded from the corrected exposed-field list, so this does not support a secret-custody finding.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Mathspace had a process for identifying and escalating vulnerability advisories. A critical advisory and patched versions existed for its deployed Metabase component, yet Mathspace states that the process did not identify and escalate that advisory before exploitation. The applicable warning process therefore failed to become operative when the published advisory should have triggered it.

The provider confirms actual personal-record download affecting 1,079,819 people including students, with specified identity/account fields. Retained privacy S4 rests on real large-scale exposure. The conventional reporting database is not established as an AI lifecycle process; students’ age does not automatically create a human-facing AI protective-response failure. Relational-role and heightened-protection tests independently completed.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The access-enforcement proposition requires approved logical-access authorisations to be enforced for information and system resources. The observed information operation was outside the approved boundary. The attacker downloaded personal information from Mathspace’s reporting database. The affected records were restricted school-user information, not public statistics. This is a bounded retrospective comparison with the selected control proposition, not a claim of certification or an independently binding historical duty.
